content.body:
## What happened

While validating #74's live behavior on staging post-merge (PR #82), found that R7 in
`specs/2026-08-09-multitenancy-slice3c-auth-cookie-scoping/requirements.md` specified
`trustedOrigins` should include **every** `VendorDomain` host (so any vendor's origin is trusted
by any other vendor's auth endpoint). Live testing on staging showed the actual deployed behavior
only trusts each vendor's **own** origin — same-origin sign-in attempts succeed (401 wrong
password), a cross-vendor origin (`srimart-staging.nocaped.com` sent to
`staging.aheedfoodcentre.nocaped.com`) is rejected (403 `INVALID_ORIGIN`), same as a genuinely
unknown origin — even though the `VendorDomain` row for SriMart demonstrably exists (its storefront
resolves correctly with distinct branding).

## Why the narrow behavior is actually correct

Blanket-trusting every vendor's origin on every other vendor's auth endpoint reopens a
cross-tenant CSRF-adjacent surface that "isolated-by-default" (the direction confirmed for slice
3c) was meant to close — a page served from SriMart's origin shouldn't be a trusted CSRF origin
for POSTing to Aheed's `/api/auth/*` endpoints. There's no current use case requiring it; the
config-gated family-SSO path already exists for the one case where cross-origin trust between
related hosts is actually wanted.

## Fix

Confirmed with the human: keep the narrow (same-origin-only, + family wildcard when armed)
behavior, and correct the spec/code to describe it deliberately instead of leaving it as
unexplained/undocumented behavior. `buildAuthOrigin`/`resolveAuthOrigin` no longer need a DB call
at all (the only DB use was populating the now-removed cross-vendor trustedOrigins entries).

Follow-up to #74, discovered during that slice's own `/ship` staging verification.
content.title: Fix: narrow auth trustedOrigins to same-vendor-only (ADR-004 slice 3c correction)

content.body:
Considered during ADR-004 slice 4 (#73) and deferred to the P6 era.

**Idea:** a curated `Theme` catalogue — named, reusable themes (each = the 8 `--color-brand-*` primitives) that a vendor **picks** from, instead of storing 8 raw hex values per vendor in `VendorBranding`.

**Why deferred (not dropped):**
- **No performance reason to rush it.** Every request is single-tenant (host→one vendor), so branding is one indexed read regardless of vendor count — flat in N for both the raw-primitives and catalogue designs. A catalogue adds at most one join.
- **Additive, not a rewrite.** The CSS-var injection seam is identical either way (components read semantic tokens; we inject 8 primitives). Introducing a `Theme` table + `VendorBranding.themeId` FK later — optionally keeping per-vendor overrides — reuses the whole slice-4 mechanism with zero throwaway work.
- **Payoff needs an admin surface.** Curation, cross-vendor reuse, and a pick-list only matter once there's a **P6** admin/onboarding UI to choose a theme; today "pick a theme" and "store 8 hex" are the same seed action.

**Scope when built:** `Theme` table (name + 8 primitives), `themeId` FK, seed a few themes, join in the branding read path, and a picker in the admin panel (P6). ~half a day of data/logic plus the UI.
content.title: Theme catalogue: named reusable themes vendors pick from (P6-era, additive to ADR-004 slice 4)

**ADR-004 slice 3c** — the outstanding piece of slice 3, deferred by slice 3b (#70) and not previously tracked. Surfaced during the slice-4 orient pass.

Implements **ADR-004 decision 4** (`specs/decisions/ADR-004-multi-tenancy.md`): auth cookie scoping derived from the `Vendor` table, not hardcoded.
- **Family SSO:** within `.aheedfoodcentre.nocaped.com`, set the session cookie on the **parent domain** → SSO across all subdomain vendors; every family subdomain in Better Auth `trustedOrigins`.
- **Custom-domain isolation:** a vendor on its own registrable domain gets an isolated session (own cookie; separate login).
- **Data-driven:** cookie `Domain` + `trustedOrigins` derived from `Vendor`/`VendorDomain` at runtime via the slice-3b resolver seam — never hardcoded (else onboarding a domain needs a deploy, violating ADR §7).

**Current state:** `lib/auth.ts` has **no** `trustedOrigins` / cookie-domain / cross-subdomain config — cookies are single-origin today.

**Sequencing:** ADR-004 sequences this **before P3**. Owner elected to build slice 4 (branding) first and circle back to 3c; this issue keeps it on the board. Cross-domain *federated* SSO remains deferred (ADR "Deferred upgrade").

content.body:
## Goal
Evolve the platform from single-vendor (hardcoded Aheed / Milton Keynes) to **multi-tenant**: regions, locations, vendors, delivery areas, and branding all come from the **database**, so a new vendor can be onboarded without code changes, each with their own branding/UI over shared business logic and data.

Design decision captured in **ADR-004 (draft)**.

## Why now (sequencing)
Do this **before P3 (cart/checkout/orders)**. Orders, carts, and payments will otherwise bake in single-vendor assumptions (an order belongs to a vendor; payment routing/payouts are per-vendor), and retrofitting vendor scoping after P3–P6 is far more expensive.

## Flagged areas (from the 2026-08-07 audit)
- **No `Vendor`/`Tenant` entity** in `prisma/schema.prisma`; no `vendorId` on `Category`/`Product`/`Inventory`/`Review`/(future `Order`).
- **Region/delivery hardcoded**: `lib/delivery.ts` (`MK1–MK19`), locality copy in header/hero/metadata.
- **Brand identity hardcoded**: `components/layout/Header.tsx` (logo + copy), `app/layout.tsx`, `app/manifest.ts`, auth pages, `lib/auth.ts` email subjects, `public/images/brand/logo.png`.
- **Design tokens**: `design-system/tokens/tokens.css` is one global theme — the two-layer (primitive→semantic) design maps cleanly to per-vendor primitives injected as CSS vars at request time.
- **Storage namespacing**: keys like `products/{slug}/...` + single `CDN_BASE_URL` — need per-vendor prefixes.
- **Config layering**: `lib/config.ts` treats brand/locality/sender as single env values — split platform config (infra) from vendor config (DB).
- **Category taxonomy/icons**: `components/product/category-icon.ts` hardcoded slug→icon map.

## Cross-cutting decisions (in the ADR)
1. **Tenant resolution** — custom domain vs subdomain vs path prefix.
2. **Data isolation** — row-level `vendorId` + enforced filtering vs schema-per-tenant.
3. **Theming delivery** — per-vendor primitives → CSS variables.
4. **Onboarding** — new vendor = data only, no deploy.

## Also surfaced
- **Staging and production currently share one Neon database** (confirmed 2026-08-07 — identical `db.checkedAt`). Multi-tenancy and environment isolation should be resolved together; a bad staging migration/seed currently hits prod.

## Deliverable
ADR-004 approved, then a dedicated foundation phase (schema + repository scoping + theming + config split) inserted before P3.

content.body:
The seven-stage SDD sequence (Orient -> Propose -> Spec -> Build -> Validate -> Document -> Ship) validates the artifact in the same context that built it. That context remembers the intent and reads it back into the code, which is the weakest possible position for Gate 3.

Restructure `specs/sdd-workflow.md` into a loop with two deliberate context resets:

**Orient -> Propose -> Spec -> Build -> Document (build notes) -> CLEAR -> Validate <-> Fix -> Ship -> Document (final) -> CLEAR -> Orient**

- Clear before Validate, switching to Sonnet 5; validation loads `requirements.md` + `validation.md` + the artifact, and treats `build-notes.md` as supporting context only.
- Clear after the final documentation pass, switching back to Opus 5, returning to Orient.
- Document splits in two: `/build-notes` (write-to-disk before the Clear, and where **Gate 4's CHANGELOG entry** now lands, since Ship precedes the final pass) and `/document` (post-ship durable record incl. KMS index and roadmap).
- New `/fix` command formalises the Validate <-> Fix cycle.

Both Clears and every model switch are user-invoked; the assistant must ask rather than proceed.
content.title: SDD workflow v2: restructure into a delivery loop with two context Clears

content.body:
## Context

While live-validating P3c (#99)'s confirmation email (R18), a real order's webhook fired correctly and the email send was genuinely attempted (`lib/email.ts` -> Resend REST API), but Resend rejected it:

\`\`\`
email send failed: 422 {\"statusCode\":422,\"name\":\"validation_error\",\"message\":\"Invalid \`to\` field. Please use our testing email address instead of domains like \`example.com\`. See our documentation for more information.\"}
\`\`\`

This is Resend's own sandbox-mode restriction (no verified sending domain on the account yet), not an application bug. `RESEND_API_KEY`/`RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` (`no-reply@aheedfoodcentre.nocaped.com`) are correctly configured as Cloudflare Worker secrets on staging, and the code path (webhook -> confirm -> `sendOrderConfirmationEmail`) worked exactly as designed, including failing gracefully without blocking order confirmation (see #99's R19, now confirmed live).

Until a sending domain is verified in Resend, **no confirmation email can reach a real customer inbox in any environment** \u2014 only Resend's own designated test address. This blocks:
- Full live verification of P3c's R18 (email content/delivery)
- Any real order confirmation email in production once P3c reaches `main`

## What's needed (owner action \u2014 Resend dashboard + DNS)

- Verify `aheedfoodcentre.nocaped.com` (or a subdomain) as a sending domain in Resend (adds DNS records: SPF/DKIM, possibly DMARC).
- Once verified, re-run a live order to confirm the email actually arrives with correct content (completes R18).

## Acceptance

A real order placed against staging results in a delivered confirmation email at a real inbox, with correct order number, line items, and vendor sender name.
content.title: Resend account needs a verified sending domain before real customer emails can be delivered

content.body:
Deferred from **P3c — Stripe payments** (#99).

P3c's order lifecycle depends entirely on Stripe's webhook being delivered. If it never arrives —
Stripe outage, endpoint misconfigured after a deploy, signing secret rotated without updating
`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` — an order stays `PENDING_PAYMENT` indefinitely and **its stock stays held**,
even though the customer may well have paid.

Stripe retries for up to ~3 days, so this is genuinely unlikely. But the failure is silent and the
consequence is real (held stock, and a paying customer with no confirmation), so it shouldn't rest
on retries alone.

Proposed: a scheduled sweep (Cloudflare Cron Trigger) that finds `PENDING_PAYMENT` orders older than
some threshold, queries Stripe for the session's actual status, and reconciles — confirm if paid,
release if expired/failed.

Home: **P7 — Compliance & hardening**, alongside the other monitoring/backup work. Worth pairing
with an alert on "orders stuck in PENDING_PAYMENT for more than N hours", since that signal catches
a misconfigured webhook far faster than a customer complaint.
content.title: Reconciliation sweep for Stripe webhooks that never arrive

content.body:
Deferred from **P3c — Stripe payments** (#99), recorded rather than half-built.

If a shopper abandons Stripe Checkout (closes the tab, back button, card declined mid-flow), their
order sits at `PENDING_PAYMENT` holding stock until the Checkout session expires and the webhook
releases it. There is no way to *resume* paying that order — the shopper has to build the cart again
and check out from scratch.

A "pay now" path would need: a route that recreates a Checkout Session for an existing
`PENDING_PAYMENT` order, guarded so it can't be used on a `CONFIRMED`/`CANCELLED` one, plus a
decision about whether the original session should be cancelled first (Stripe allows multiple live
sessions for the same order, which risks a double charge if both are completed).

That last point is why this wasn't built inline: it's a correctness question about money, and it
deserves its own thinking rather than being tacked onto P3c.

Not blocking anything — the current behaviour is safe, just inconvenient.
content.title: Resume payment for an order stuck in PENDING_PAYMENT

content.body:
Third slice of **P3 — Cart & checkout** (epic #86), following P3b (#96). Swaps the stub
`PaymentService` for real Stripe, closing the gap P3b explicitly left open: stock held by an
abandoned checkout has no release path until this slice.

## 🛑 Hard blocker — no Stripe credentials exist anywhere
Checked: staging secrets, production secrets, local `.env`/`.dev.vars` — all empty. **The owner
must create a Stripe account (or use an existing one) and provide test-mode keys** before this can
be validated end-to-end. Per environment (staging + production), as Cloudflare Worker secrets:
- `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`
- `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`
- `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`

Spec and most of the build can proceed against Stripe's documented API without these (mirroring how
P3b was built and unit-tested with a stub before any keys existed); only final live/staging
validation is blocked.

## Scope
- **Real `PaymentService` adapter** (`lib/payments.ts`) creating a hosted Stripe Checkout session via
  raw `fetch()` to Stripe's REST API — **not the `stripe` npm SDK**, matching this repo's established
  pattern (`aws4fetch` over the AWS SDK, plain `fetch` over Resend's SDK, both for Worker bundle
  size). ADR-005's single-platform-account decision is unchanged; `vendorId` continues to flow
  through for the future Connect seam.
- **Signature-verified, idempotent webhook** (`app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts`, Node runtime).
  Idempotency reuses the **conditional-update guard pattern** from P3b's stock decrement (`WHERE
  status = 'PENDING_PAYMENT'` on the transition) — no new event-log table, same proven technique.
- **Stock release on payment failure / Checkout session expiry** — the order moves to `CANCELLED`
  (existing enum value, no schema change) and each line's `Inventory.quantity` is incremented back.
  This is the gap P3b recorded and must not ship ahead of.
- **The success_url is the existing `/checkout/{orderNumber}` confirmation page**, made
  status-aware. Stripe's own guidance: the client redirect is never the source of truth (closed tab,
  race with the webhook) — the page renders whatever `order.status` actually is (`PENDING_PAYMENT` →
  "confirming your payment…", `CONFIRMED` → today's confirmation, `CANCELLED` → failure messaging).
  No new route.
- **Confirmation email fires only from the webhook**, once status flips to `CONFIRMED` — never at
  order creation (owner decision, 2026-08-10). Matches this codebase's consistent "never assume
  money" pattern (P3b's server-side-only totals, the stock decrement's atomicity). A guest sees a
  short delay between placing the order and the email; the email is never wrong.

## Explicitly NOT in this slice
- Cash on Delivery — out of scope entirely (P3b decision, unchanged).
- Delivery slots — P4.
- "Shop your list" — P3d.
- Stripe Connect / per-vendor payout routing — deferred upgrade per ADR-005.

## Acceptance criteria
None here — per Gate 2 they live in `specs/<YYYY-MM-DD-p3c-*>/validation.md` once the spec is
written.

content.body:
Follow-up from validating **P3b — checkout + order core** (#96) live on staging.

## What's true today
SriMart's `/checkout` on `srimart-staging.nocaped.com` correctly renders its own theme, locality
and delivery fee with **zero per-vendor code branches** — the architecture claim (ADR-004's rule of
thumb: onboarding/config changes are data-only) is proven. But the delivery *value* shown is
`£3.49`, which is `VendorConfig.deliveryFeePence`'s **schema default** (`349`), not the
SriMart-specific values seeded in `prisma/seed.ts` (`deliveryFeePence: 299`,
`freeDeliveryThresholdPence: 5000`, `minimumOrderPence: 1000`).

## Why
`prisma/seed.ts` only touches SriMart's vendor/catalogue/satellites when **both**
`SEED_AHEED_HOST` and `SEED_SRIMART_HOST` are set (a deliberate safety design — see the seed
script's own log line, `"SEED_SRIMART_HOST set but SEED_AHEED_HOST is not — skipping SriMart to
stay safe"`). The `npm run db:seed` run that populated Aheed's P3a delivery columns had neither set,
so SriMart's `VendorConfig` row was never touched and is running on migration defaults.

## Fix
Re-run the seed against staging with both host vars set, per `docs/env-setup.md`'s existing pattern:

```
DIRECT_URL="<staging DIRECT_URL>" \
SEED_AHEED_HOST="staging.aheedfoodcentre.nocaped.com" \
SEED_SRIMART_HOST="srimart-staging.nocaped.com" \
npm run db:seed
```

Not urgent — the current default values are safe and sensible, and nothing is broken. This is
purely to make SriMart's demo data actually distinct from Aheed's, matching the intent of the
per-vendor seed values already written in `prisma/seed.ts`.

content.body:
Second slice of **P3 — Cart & checkout** (epic #86), following P3a (#93). Turns a cart into a real order. **No Stripe** — payment is stubbed behind the port so the riskiest logic is testable before any credential exists.

## Scope
- **Schema:** `Address`, `Order`, `OrderItem`, `Payment`, `OrderStatusEvent` — all `vendorId`-scoped per ADR-004 (which names `Order` explicitly). Reuses the `OrderStatus`/`PaymentStatus` enums and the `Order`/`OrderItem` shape already sketched in `specs/architecture.md` §3.2, which predates tenancy and needs `vendorId` added.
- **Totals from vendor data:** subtotal, `deliveryFeePence`, `freeDeliveryThresholdPence`, `minimumOrderPence` (all landed in P3a's `VendorConfig`). No constants.
- **Deliverability gate:** checkout refuses a postcode outside the vendor's `VendorDeliveryArea`, reusing the pure `isDeliverable(postcode, prefixes)`.
- **Atomic order creation with stock decrement** — the core of this slice. Conditional `updateMany` guard inside an interactive transaction, **no raw SQL** (CLAUDE.md):
  ```ts
  const { count } = await tx.inventory.updateMany({
    where: { productId, vendorId, quantity: { gte: qty } },
    data:  { quantity: { decrement: qty } },
  });
  if (count === 0) throw new OutOfStockError(productId);
  ```
  Postgres evaluates the guard and the write atomically, so two concurrent checkouts for the last item cannot both succeed.
- **`PaymentService` port + stub adapter** (`tech-stack.md` names the port; it has never been created). Stub marks payment `PENDING` and returns a placeholder reference — P3c swaps in Stripe behind the same interface.
- **Guest + account checkout**, following `docs/ui-ref/CheckoutModal.tsx`'s structure (colours/constants translated through `design-system.md`'s token table, never copied — same rule as P3a).
- **On-screen order confirmation** (the emailed one is P3c, with real payment).
- **ADR-005 — Payments & multi-vendor money flow**, written alongside: single platform Stripe account with a Connect-ready seam, and the merchant-of-record posture that implies.

## Decisions taken with the owner (2026-08-10)
1. **Stock decrements at order creation**, not at payment success — oversell becomes structurally impossible. Cost: an abandoned checkout holds stock until released; **release on payment-failed / session-expired is P3c** and is deliberately recorded as a gap here so it can't be forgotten.
2. **Delivery slots deferred to P4.** The reference has a slot picker, but slots done properly need per-vendor windows, capacity and cutoffs — otherwise 40 deliveries sell into one 2-hour window. P4 is where delivery is already the subject.
3. **Card only — no Cash on Delivery.** Matches the roadmap. COD is a second order lifecycle (CONFIRMED but unpaid) plus cash reconciliation; if wanted it deserves its own proposal.

## Explicitly NOT in this slice
- Stripe, webhooks, emailed confirmation — **P3c**
- "Shop your list" — **P3d**
- Delivery slots/capacity — **P4**
- Cash on Delivery — out of scope entirely
- Order history / status transitions / staff updates — **P4**

## Inherited from P3a
- **The merge prompt must be forced to resolution before an order is created** (`specs/2026-08-09-p3a-cart-foundation/plan.md` open items) — an order must never be placed against a cart the shopper never confirmed.

## Acceptance criteria
None here — per Gate 2 they live in `specs/<YYYY-MM-DD-p3b-checkout-order-core>/validation.md` once the spec is written.

## Operational prerequisite
Staging's `VendorConfig` delivery columns are still `NULL` (added in P3a's migration; values come from seed). A staging re-seed is needed before totals can be verified end-to-end.

content.body:
Deferred from **P3a — cart foundation** (#93), recorded rather than left as a code comment.

Guest carts are created lazily (only on a first add) and keyed by an opaque cookie token, but
**nothing ever reaps them**. Volume is ~zero today, so this is not a P3a problem — but it is a real
long-term data-growth issue, and a guest cart is weakly personal data (it links a browser to a set
of product interests).

Likely home: **P7 — Compliance & hardening**, alongside the UK GDPR retention review, so the
retention window is decided once for all weakly-personal data rather than ad hoc here.

Options to weigh at that point:
- a scheduled reaper (Cloudflare Cron Trigger) deleting guest carts untouched for N days
- a `Cart.updatedAt` sweep folded into an existing job
- relying on cookie expiry alone (currently 30 days) — leaves orphaned rows, so probably not enough

Not blocking anything.

content.body:
`secrets/production.vars` currently contains **staging''s** `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, byte-identical to `secrets/staging.vars` (verified by hash). The production Cloudflare Worker has the **correct** per-endpoint value, set manually via the Cloudflare dashboard.

**Why this is now live rather than latent:** before PR #109, `configure-env.mjs` did not know these keys and silently skipped them, so the stale file value was unreachable. #109 taught it to push them. Running `node scripts/configure-env.mjs production` now would overwrite the Worker''s correct secret with staging''s.

**Failure mode if that happens is silent.** Every Stripe delivery to the production endpoint fails signature verification, the handler returns before doing anything, and orders never leave `PENDING_PAYMENT` — with their stock decremented and never released, because release happens on webhook events that are now all rejected.

**Fix (owner action):** copy the signing secret for `https://aheedfoodcentre.nocaped.com/api/webhooks/stripe` from the Stripe dashboard into `secrets/production.vars`. The Stripe API does not return the signing secret for an already-created endpoint, so the dashboard is the only source.

Documented in `docs/env-setup.md` 1.7.0 (per-endpoint warning) and PR #110.

content.body:
PR #108 (`staging → main`) used `Closes #93, #96, #99, #106`. Only **#93** closed on merge. #96 and #99 shipped to production and stayed open until closed by hand; #106 closed separately, via the `Closes #106` in commit `aa39d67`''s own message reaching `main`.

GitHub only honours the closing keyword for the **first** issue in a comma-separated list. Each issue needs its own keyword:

```
closes #93, closes #96, closes #99, closes #106
```

**Why it matters here specifically:** this repo merges PRs into `staging`, which is not the default branch, so closing keywords never fire on a slice PR. Every issue closure is deferred to the `staging → main` promotion PR — which means promotion PRs routinely carry several `Closes` references at once, and are exactly where this bug bites. The board''s `Item closed → Done` workflow then never fires, so shipped work silently sits in the wrong status.

**Fix:** add a line to `.claude/commands/ship.md` and the Ship section of `specs/sdd-workflow.md` requiring the keyword to be repeated per issue on promotion PRs.

content.body:
Production currently runs Stripe in **test mode**. `secrets/production.vars` holds an `sk_test_…`
secret key and a `pk_test_…` publishable key that are **byte-identical to staging's** (verified by
hash comparison — same Stripe account, same keys, two environments).

This is deliberate and correct for today: P3a/P3b/P3c were promoted to production ahead of the
storefront opening precisely so that no real money could move. It is recorded in `specs/roadmap.md`
as prose in the P3-promotion change-log row.

**Why this needs its own issue.** The other two launch blockers are tracked (#104 Resend verified
sending domain, #103 payment-failure-path live verification). The live-key swap is named only inside
a roadmap paragraph, so it is the blocker most likely to be assumed as someone else's job. It is
also the one that cannot be discovered by testing — a test-mode production storefront takes
payments that look successful and settle nothing.

**Owner actions when the storefront is ready to open (all dashboard-only, no code change):**

- [ ] Activate the live Stripe account (business details, bank account, verification).
- [ ] Put the **live** `sk_live_…` / `pk_live_…` into `secrets/production.vars` — these must NOT
      match staging; staging stays on test keys permanently.
- [ ] Create a **live-mode** webhook endpoint for `https://aheedfoodcentre.nocaped.com/api/webhooks/stripe`
      and copy its own signing secret into `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Live and test endpoints have
      **different** signing secrets — this is the same per-endpoint trap as #111.
- [ ] `node scripts/configure-env.mjs production`, then redeploy the Worker.
- [ ] Verify with one real low-value payment end-to-end, then refund it.

**Do not do this before #104 is resolved** — a live order whose confirmation email cannot be
delivered is a real customer with no receipt.

Related: #104, #103, #111. Surfaced during `/orient` on 2026-08-10.

content.body:
**The last P3 slice.** P3a/P3b/P3c delivered cart → checkout → payment; P3's scope
(`specs/roadmap.md`) also folds in **"Shop your list"** as a cart-entry path. P3 cannot close
until this ships.

## What it is

A shopper pastes or types a shopping list, each line is matched against the vendor's catalogue,
they review the matches, and one click adds the confirmed lines to the existing cart.

## Decisions taken at Propose (confirmed with the human)

**1. Matching — token-AND on product name, no new infrastructure.**
Each line is parsed for a leading/trailing quantity, the remainder is split into tokens, and a
product must match **all** tokens in its `name` (Prisma `AND` of `contains`, insensitive). Ranked
exact-name > all-tokens > partial.

The existing `ProductRepository.search()` is a single `contains` OR'd across `name`/`description` —
`"chicken breast"` finds *Halal Chicken Breast*, but `"2x chicken breast 500g"` finds nothing. That
is exactly the input this feature invites, so list matching needs its own repository method rather
than reusing `search()`.

**Rejected: Postgres `pg_trgm` similarity.** It would handle typos (`bannanas` → *Bananas*), but
querying it requires `$queryRaw`, which `CLAUDE.md` forbids in application code, and P2 deliberately
deferred trigram search until the catalogue outgrows placeholder data. Not worth reversing two
standing decisions for one slice. **Typos are therefore explicitly out of scope** — a mistyped line
reports as unmatched, which the review step makes visible rather than silent.

**2. Stateless — no new tables, no migration.**
Paste → match → review → add, in one pass. The cart *is* the persistence. A saved
`ShoppingList` aggregate (reusable weekly lists) is a real feature but a retention one, closer to
P5 than to P3's cart-entry path; it would add an aggregate, a migration, account-area UI and
guest-vs-user ownership rules. P3d adds **zero schema change**, so it cannot collide with P4's
order work.

**3. Every line is reviewed before anything enters the cart.**
Matched lines appear pre-selected with their parsed quantity, ambiguous lines show a chooser,
unmatched lines are flagged — then one explicit "Add N items" action. Nothing is auto-added.
Ambiguity is real in this catalogue, not hypothetical: `milk` matches both *Whole Milk* and
*Coconut Milk*. A confidently-wrong silent add is only discovered at checkout, or at the door.

## Prerequisites — verified present at `/orient`, not assumed

- `features/cart/add-to-cart.ts` — server action; `addItem(identity, productId, qty)` already
  takes a quantity, so bulk add reuses it rather than adding a parallel write path.
- `lib/repositories/cart.ts` — vendor-scoped, guest-or-user identity (P3a).
- `lib/cart-rules.ts` — `effectiveStock()` / `clampQuantity()`; out-of-stock and over-stock lines
  must go through these, not re-derive the maths.
- `lib/repositories/products.ts` — where the new list-matching method belongs (vendor scoping and
  the `isActive` filter are already enforced there).

## Scope boundaries

**In:** list entry UI, line parsing (quantity + tokens), a vendor-scoped matching repository method,
the review screen (matched / ambiguous / unmatched / out-of-stock), bulk add to the existing cart.

**Out:** saved lists, typo tolerance, trigram/fuzzy search, barcode or photo input, reordering from
a past order (that is P4, once order history exists), any schema change.

## Gates

Spec at `specs/2026-08-11-p3d-shop-your-list/` (plan + requirements + validation) before any code.
Line parsing and ranking must be **pure and unit-tested** without a DB — same split as
`lib/cart-rules.ts`, `lib/auth-origin.ts` and `lib/delivery.ts`. DB-touching validation runs under
`npm run preview`, never `npm run dev`.

Closes P3 once shipped and promoted.

content.body:
P3d (#114) matches a list line by **token-AND on product name**: a product must contain *every*
term the line produced. That makes `2x chicken breast` → *Halal Chicken Breast*, but it also makes
this unmatched:

```
chicken breast 500g   → no product name contains BOTH "breast" AND "500g"
```

The shopper sees an explicit "no match", which is honest and by design — the review step exists so
nothing wrong is silently added. But a line that names a real product **plus a size the catalogue
does not carry in its name** is a plausible thing to type off a handwritten list, and reporting it
as absent is not the most useful answer available.

**Possible approach (not decided):** when a line has no all-terms match, fall back to the largest
matching term subset and offer those as an *ambiguous* line rather than `unmatched` — the shopper
still confirms, so nothing is auto-added. This deliberately was **not** built into P3d because it
contradicts R9 (`a product matches only when its name contains every term`), and quietly widening
an approved spec mid-build is exactly what the SDD gates exist to prevent.

**Related but distinct:** typo tolerance (`bannanas` → *Bananas*) is a different problem, needing
`pg_trgm` and therefore `$queryRaw` — forbidden in application code by `CLAUDE.md`, and deferred at
P2 until the catalogue outgrows placeholder data. That is not what this issue asks for; term-subset
fallback needs no new extension and no raw SQL.

Also worth revisiting here: term matching is currently **substring, not word-boundary**, which is
harmless at 16 seeded products but will produce odd matches as the catalogue grows.

Surfaced during `/build` of P3d. Needs its own `/propose`.
content.title: Shop your list: no partial-match fallback — a line naming a real product plus an unknown size reports unmatched

content.body:
P3d (#114) shipped "Shop your list" as a **stateless** cart-entry path: paste → match → review →
add, in one pass. The cart is the persistence; the typed list itself is not stored anywhere.

A shopper who buys roughly the same things every week retypes the list every week. Saving it would
be a genuine retention feature.

**Why it was excluded from P3d** (recorded in `specs/2026-08-10-p3d-shop-your-list/plan.md`): it
needs a new `ShoppingList` / `ShoppingListItem` aggregate, a migration, account-area UI, and rules
for what happens to a guest's list when they sign in. That is a phase-sized feature sitting closer
to **P5 (loyalty & discounts)** than to P3's cart-entry path, and P3d deliberately shipped with
**zero schema change** so it could not collide with P4's order work.

**When to reconsider:** P4 adds order history, which makes "reorder my last order" the more natural
first version of this — it needs no new tables at all and probably supersedes half of what a saved
list is for. Worth sequencing that first and seeing what demand is left.

Not scheduled. Needs its own `/propose` before any spec.
